recap.workouts:
Three pieces, all of them deliberately cheap, and the protected day did exactly what it was built to do.

06:00 — The Laestrygonians. 85 minutes in the gym, average HR 111, max 144, load 24, RPE 5. Your note: 400 m runs, 20 lb dumbbells for the lunges, easy pace on the burpees. So you ran the [TRAIN] distance and scaled the loaded piece below even the [FITNESS] call — and the loaded piece was the whole point. Three hundred feet of walking lunges was the one thing on today's card that could still be in your legs on Saturday, and you took it at 20 lb. An average of 111 across eighty-five minutes with a ceiling of 144 says the rest was genuinely cruised.

Upper pull and triceps in the same visit, all five movements at three sets — Back 6, Biceps 3, Rear Delts 3, Triceps 3, which is week 10's engine target for this day served exactly.

Lat pulldown 190 — 12, 12, 12. Top of the range on all three sets.
Barbell row 80 — 12, 10, 9. First session on the bumped load, all three inside 8-12.
Barbell curl — 45 × 12, then you put it up to 55 for 10 and 12.
Face pull 85 — 20, 20, 20. Top of the range on all three.
Overhead triceps extension 130 — 12, 12, 12. Top of the range on all three, first session on the bump.

RRe3 — 29:38, 4.81 km, load 25 against a planned 23, paired at 108.7% compliance, RPE 3. Average HR 126, max 146, against a run threshold of 167.

By kilometre split:
km 1 — 5:51/km, HR 113, running about 2% downhill (the strap took the first twenty seconds to find you, so that average sits low)
km 2 — 5:54/km, HR 121
km 3 — 6:09/km, HR 125, ground turning flat
km 4 — 6:31/km, HR 134, with 21 m of climbing inside that kilometre
km 5 (0.81 km) — 6:27/km, HR 132

Zone 1 is 5:45-7:17/km and 121-135 bpm. Every split sat inside both. The pace stepped down exactly as the ground tilted up — average gradient across the five splits went -2.1%, -1.4%, +0.3%, +2.1%, +1.2% — and heart rate as a share of threshold went 67, 72, 74, 80, 79 percent. That is a terrain profile, not a fatigue one. The 146 peak came on the steepest kilometre and is the only moment all session that reached into Zone 2 by heart rate.

Your note: conversational pace, on a call with a colleague. That is the correct way to run this session, and the file agrees with you.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: proceed. RRe3 was executed as written and then some — 108.7% compliance, load 25 against 23, every kilometre inside the Zone 1 pace band and inside the Zone 1 heart rate band, and the only variation in the trace is the hill. Nothing in it flags fatigue and nothing in it needs answering. Confidence high: the session paired cleanly and the splits come straight off the activity file. Worth noting that intervals.icu is now scoring you against LTHR 167 — the per-split intensity figures line up to the beat with the run anchor RT19 established, so the tune has propagated properly.

2) Two load triggers fired tonight, both on the all-sets rule. Lat pulldown 190 × 12/12/12 → 200. Overhead triceps extension 130 × 12/12/12 → 140, and that one on the first session at the bumped load. Face pull put three of its six weekly sets at the top of the range; Thursday's three decide whether 85 goes to 90. Barbell row holds at 80 — 12, 10, 9 is the first session on a new load and the reps fell across the sets.

3) You promoted the curl yourself, and the number is right. 45 × 12 then 55 for 10 and 12 clears the 8-12 range on both heavier sets, so the card's 45 is already stale. Run 55 tomorrow, not 45 — and 12 on all three at 55 is what takes it to 60.

4) ADAPT: no-op. CrossFit, hypertrophy and RRe3 all classify as EXECUTED. Nothing in the remaining week moves. Four endurance sessions left in week 10 and the two that matter — Thursday's pyramid and Saturday's 150 — are both still in front of you, which is exactly the state today was supposed to hand over.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

15′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W → 35′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W → 10′ Zone 1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 9 Aug.)
Read the shape — CF10 is not CF9. The Zone 1 opener is fifteen minutes and the cool-down is ten, so the Zone 2 block is only 35 minutes long.
This ride carries the week's 10′ @ 165 W reference block. It replaces 10 minutes of the Zone 2 block, so the session is still 60 minutes: 10′ @ 165 W + 25′ Zone 2. Regenerate the file with python make_zwo.py CF10 --ref-block — it pins the FTP override so Zwift's own stored number can't shift the target.
165 W is a fixed wattage, not a zone. It does not move when FTP is tuned, and that is the entire point: it is the only repeated measure the progress track has, and it is what will finally give the bike a proper test-retest error. Hold it flat and let the heart rate say whatever it says — the value is in the conditions repeating, not in the watts being impressive.
Monday is the right day for it. The block wants a repeatable, unremarkable condition, and the first easy day of the week off a weekend is exactly that — far better than squeezing it in beside a hard session later on.

end.name: RMI1 — 36′ mixed-intensity pyramid
end.desc:
Library structure, verbatim: 5′ Z1, 5′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km, 1′ Zone 5 (faster than 3:48/km), 2′ Z1, 3′ Zone 4 @ 3:48–4:17/km, 2′ Z1, 5′ Zone 3 @ 4:22–4:42/km, 2′ Z1, 3′ Zone 4, 2′ Z1, 1′ Zone 5, 5′ Z1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 9 Aug.)
Read the shape before you start: this is a pyramid, not a repeat set — every rep is a different zone. 1′ hard, 3′ at Zone 4, 5′ at threshold, 3′ at Zone 4, 1′ hard. The classic failure is running rep 3 at rep 2's pace, which turns the Zone 5 minutes into Zone 4 and the Zone 3 block into Zone X.
Run the recoveries honestly — a full 2′ Zone 1 between everything. The 5′ Zone 3 block in the middle is the anchor; run it on the run-measured anchors and expect to sit near LTHR 167.
Total hard content is 13 minutes inside 36 — small by design, because Saturday is the week's deliverable and Friday is a pure Zone 1 spin between the two.

You rode this exact interval content last Wednesday and it was the best threshold session of the block: block 1 at 225 W, block 2 at 235 W and cleaner than block 1, all ten Z4 reps at 263–265 W, 0.0 minutes of Zone X. The two 20′ blocks are not a step into the unknown — only the 30 extra Zone 1 minutes are. Target 222–235 W on block 1 and let block 2 answer for itself; if HR plateaus clearly under 159, ride it a touch firmer exactly as you did.
Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step.
On-bike gate for the Z4 set: if you cannot get back to Z1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set there and spin out the rest. Ending on seven good reps is a completed session; grinding out ten bad ones is not.
The 30′ Zone 1 tail is Zone 1 and only Zone 1 — 118–165 W. It is the whole difference between CMI1 and CMI2 and the cheapest aerobic half hour on the card; ride it at 180 W and it becomes half an hour of Zone X tax on the hardest day of the week.
If Saturday arrives flat, slide this to Sunday and drop RF12. Never water it down into a medium ride — that is full fatigue cost for no adaptation.

2026-08-16.mind: Ninety minutes inside the band, and holding the band when my legs want to drift faster is the actual work today — the week is already won or lost, so all that is left is not spending it.

end.name: RF12 — 90′ long easy run, closes the week
end.desc:
5′ Z1 → 80′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 5′ Z1. (Verified library structure.)
This is the session that cost week 9 its 80/20 badge — 14.7 of the week's 19.4 Zone X minutes came from this exact workout last Saturday. Nothing about it needs to change except the discipline.
Run it off the MIDDLE of the band — around 5:18–5:25/km — not the 5:01 edge. That was the instruction last week and it worked: you ran 5:23 for eighty minutes and never put a second above 150 bpm. The Zone X minutes were a hill doing it to you on the downhill half at 133–144 bpm, which cost nothing. That was terrain being generous. Don't go looking for the band on purpose. 5:01/km is a wall, not a target.
Ninety minutes of honest Zone 2 the day after 150 minutes on the bike is a hard thing to do slowly. Do it slowly — this is the taper of intensity, not of hours, and it is the last of seven straight training days.
This is the day the week gives back if Saturday slid. If CMI2 moves to Sunday, this run comes out entirely.
